classification.difficultyReason: Recognise two identical circular segments and subtract a right-angled triangle from each quadrant.

inlines.text: Work out the area of the shaded region. Answer to 2 decimal places.
(Hint: use the area of a triangle!)

spec.description: An upright square with external left and bottom dimensions of 16 cm. Two quarter-circle arcs join the top-left and bottom-right corners; their intervening lens is shaded.
spec.mathematics: Square side 16 cm. The arcs have radius 16 cm and centres at the bottom-left and top-right corners. The lens consists of two identical quadrant-minus-triangle segments.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens and the requested shaded region are visible; no calculated areas are shown.

answer.worked:
Each segment is a quadrant minus a right-angled triangle.
$$\begin{align*}
A_{\text{segment}} &= \frac14\pi(16)^2-\frac12(16)(16)\\
A_{\text{segment}} &= 64\pi-128\\
A_{\text{segment}} &\approx 73.06\text{ cm}^2
\end{align*}$$
There are two identical segments. Use the exact segment area before rounding.
$$\begin{align*}
A_{\text{shaded}} &= 2(64\pi-128)\\
A_{\text{shaded}} &= 128\pi-256\\
A_{\text{shaded}} &\approx 146.12\text{ cm}^2
\end{align*}$$
